```{r Importing data}

# Importing time series data from Excel files
load_data <- read_excel("datasets/load.xlsx")
humidity_data <- read_excel("datasets/relative_humidity.xlsx")
temperature_data <- read_excel("datasets/temperature.xlsx")

# Inspecting the data
head(load_data)
head(humidity_data)
head(temperature_data)

```

```{r Handling missing values}

# Gaby added

summary(load_data)
# We have 6 NAs in h2

summary(humidity_data)
# No NAs in humidity data

summary(temperature_data)
# No NAs in temperature data

# Identify NAs in load data
NAs <- load_data %>% 
  filter(is.na(load_data$h2) == TRUE)
NAs
# 5 of the NAs are between 2005-2010

# Getting number of variables and observations for load
nvar <- ncol(load_data) - 1
nobs <- nrow(load_data)

# Interpolate missing values for load
load_data <- load_data %>%
        mutate(h2 = na.approx(h2))

NAcheck <- load_data %>% 
  filter(is.na(load_data$h2) == TRUE)
NAcheck

```

```{r Process the data}

# Take the mean load from h1 through h24 for each day
load_daily <- load_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Daily_Load = mean(c_across(h1:h24))) %>%
  select(date, Daily_Load)

# Take the daily averages of humidity data across sensors
humidity_daily <- humidity_data %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(Daily_Humidity = mean(c_across(starts_with("rh_ws")), na.rm = TRUE))

# Take the daily averages of temperature data across sensors
temperature_daily <- temperature_data %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(Daily_Temperature = mean(c_across(starts_with("t_ws")), na.rm = TRUE))

# Join load, humidity, and temperature variables into one data frame
daily_data <- load_daily %>%
  left_join(humidity_daily, by = "date") %>%
  left_join(temperature_daily, by = "date")

```


```{r Creating our first ts object}
# Creating our first ts object
# Using msts because our daily data has more than one seasonal component
daily_ts <- msts(daily_data$Daily_Load, 
                 seasonal.periods = c(7, 365), 
                 # start year, month, day
                 start = c(2005, 1, 1))

# Inspect the ts plot
autoplot(daily_ts) + ggtitle("Daily Load Time Series")

```

```{r Decompose the series}

# Gaby added in case we need
decompose_load <- decompose(daily_ts, "multiplicative")
plot(decompose_load)

```

```{r Create subsets for training and testing purposes}

# Gaby added
# Subset for training
# For model training, use data from January 1, 2005, to December 31, 2009.
n_for = 365

daily_ts_train <- subset(daily_ts,
                         end = length(daily_ts) - n_for)
autoplot(daily_ts_train) + ggtitle("Training subset")

# Subset for testing -- can delete if we don't end up needing
daily_ts_test <- subset(daily_ts,
                        start = length(daily_ts) - n_for)
autoplot(daily_ts_test) + ggtitle("Testing subset")

# To evaluate model performance, use the fitted models to forecast daily demand for January 1, 2010, to February 28, 2010, as a validation set.

```


```{r Arithmetic mean on original data}

# Gaby added
# Train on January 1, 2005, to December 31, 2009.
MEAN_seas_load_train <- meanf(y = daily_ts_train, h = 59)
plot(MEAN_seas_load_train)

# After selecting the best-performing model(s), re-train the model using the full dataset from January 1, 2005, to December 31, 2010. Use this updated model to generate forecasts for January 1, 2011, to February 28, 2011. The final forecasts will be submitted as part of the competition.
MEAN_seas_load_forecast <- meanf(y = daily_ts, h = 59)
plot(MEAN_seas_load_forecast)

```

```{r ETS}

ets_model <- ets(daily_ts[1:(5 * 365)])  # Training on first 5 years
ets_forecast <- forecast(ets_model, h = 59)

```

```{r TBATS}

tbats_model <- tbats(daily_ts[1:(5 * 365)])
tbats_forecast <- forecast(tbats_model, h = 59)

```

```{r ARIMA with Fourier terms}

# Fourier terms as exogenous regressors
# Fourier terms are ideal for complex seasonalities, like in the load data (both daily and hourly variation)
# P, D, and Q are 0 because seasonality will be expressed in the Fourier terms

# First, store the Fourier terms K values consistently
K_values <- c(2, 4)  # Using the same values you tried

# Fit the model with these K values
ARIMA_Four_fit <- auto.arima(daily_ts_train,
                           seasonal = FALSE,
                           lambda = 0,
                           xreg = fourier(daily_ts_train, K = K_values))

# Create Fourier terms for forecasting with the same K values
fourier_terms <- fourier(daily_ts_train, K = K_values, h = 59)

# Generate forecast using the model
ARIMA_Four_forecast <- forecast(ARIMA_Four_fit,
                              xreg = fourier_terms,
                              h = 59)  # 59 days
```


```{r}
# 1. Calculate MAPE for all models on the validation period
actual <- daily_ts[(5 * 365 + 1):(5 * 365 + 59)]

mape_snaive <- mean(abs((actual - SNAIVE_seas_train$mean) / actual)) * 100
mape_sma <- mean(abs((actual - SMA_seas_fit_train$mean) / actual)) * 100
mape_arima <- mean(abs((actual - arima_forecast$mean) / actual)) * 100
mape_ets <- mean(abs((actual - ets_forecast$mean) / actual)) * 100
mape_tbats <- mean(abs((actual - tbats_forecast$mean) / actual)) * 100

mape_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Seasonal Naive", "Simple Moving Average", "ARIMA", "ETS", "TBATS"),
  MAPE = c(mape_snaive, mape_sma, mape_arima, mape_ets, mape_tbats)
)

mape_results <- mape_results[order(mape_results$MAPE), ]
print(mape_results)

# 2. Train the best model on the full dataset and generate forecasts
best_model <- tbats(daily_ts)
best_forecast <- forecast(best_model, h = 59)

# 3. Format for submission
submission_df <- data.frame(
  date = format(seq.Date(from = as.Date("2011-01-01"), 
                   by = "day", 
                   length.out = 59), "%Y-%m-%d"),
  load = round(best_forecast$mean)
)

write.csv(submission_df, "final_submission.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
